title: RAG-Modulo: Solving Sequential Tasks using Experience, Critics, and Language Models
notes: Robotic decision-making memory paper; addresses generic inability to retain/learn from past interactions.

title: Manufacturing Domain QA with Integrated Term Enhanced RAG
notes: Domain RAG QA paper (manufacturing); addresses hallucination generically (details truncated).

title: Robust Pronoun Fidelity with English LLMs: Are they Reasoning, Repeating, or Just Biased?
notes: Introduces "pronoun fidelity" as an evaluation task for discourse coreference robustness under distractor entities; a capability/bias evaluation task, not clearly an agent-context-pollution degradation mechanism.

title: Blinded by Generated Contexts: How Language Models Merge Generated and Retrieved Contexts When Knowledge Conflicts?
notes: Diagnostic study of how LLMs merge conflicting generated vs. retrieved contexts; extends existing knowledge-conflict framing to hybrid generate+retrieve settings without introducing a new named mechanism.

title: Scalable Multi-Robot Collaboration with Large Language Models: Centralized or Decentralized Systems?
notes: Multi-robot planning architecture-comparison paper; token-budget/communication-architecture study, no new mechanism.

title: Memory Sandbox: Transparent and Interactive Memory Management for Conversational Agents
notes: HCI design-probe paper for transparent conversational memory; "distracted by irrelevant parts of the conversation" used only generically.

title: Synapse: Trajectory-as-Exemplar Prompting with Memory for Computer Control
notes: ICL-based computer-control agent paper; addresses generic context-length/exemplar-structure limitations.

title: Alleviating Contextual Misguidance: Response-Aware Prompt Compression for Long-Context Question Answering
mechanism_name: contextual misguidance
notes: Paper identifies a specific causal mechanism underlying "Lost in the Middle": query-relevant yet non-grounding/misleading spans in long context misdirect the model, distinct from mere positional forgetting -- a mechanistic refinement of the established phenomenon.

title: Cognitive Scaffold: From Fluid Context to Crystallized Memory for Long-Horizon DeepResearch Agents
notes: Memory architecture paper (details truncated); "context-noise trade-off" used generically for this system's motivation.

title: Mitigate Position Bias in LLMs via Scaling a Single Hidden States Channel
mechanism_name: mechanistic explanation of position bias / lost-in-the-middle via hidden-state positional-information channel
notes: Paper identifies a micro-level mechanistic account of position bias: attention weights as a micro-expression of position bias, and a specific hidden-state channel (beyond position embeddings) carrying positional information (details truncated but central finding is clear from abstract/title).

title: MEMORA: Embodied Action Memory from Egocentric Videos for Reasoning and Planning
notes: Embodied action-memory capability paper; error-propagation noted only briefly (details truncated).

title: Directional Attractors in LLM Reasoning: How Similarity Retrieval Steers Iterative Summarization Based Reasoning
notes: Iterative-summarization-reasoning paper; studies how retrieval steers reasoning trajectories, a capability/architecture question rather than a named degradation mechanism.

title: Cache What Lasts: Token Retention for Memory-Bounded KV Cache in LLMs
notes: KV-cache eviction paper; "premature eviction from attention-based importance proxies" is a specific technique limitation (attention bias), overlapping with recognized attention-based eviction unreliability, not clearly a new general mechanism.

title: Taming Knowledge Conflicts in Language Models
mechanism_name: superposition of contextual information and parametric memory (mechanistic explanation of knowledge conflict)
notes: Mechanistic-interpretability finding overturning the prior "exclusive memory heads vs. context heads" assumption: influential attention heads simultaneously encode both parametric and contextual signals. A mechanistic refinement of the established knowledge-conflict phenomenon.

title: SUGAR: Leveraging Contextual Confidence for Smarter Retrieval
notes: Adaptive-retrieval-triggering paper; "distracted by noisy retrieved content" used generically (established distraction framing).

title: Adaptive Chameleon or Stubborn Sloth: Revealing the Behavior of Large Language Models in Knowledge Conflicts
notes: First controlled investigation of LLM receptiveness to conflicting external evidence; systematically studies (does not newly name) the existing knowledge-conflict phenomenon.

title: Still: Amortized KV Cache Compaction in a Single Forward Pass
notes: KV-cache compaction systems paper; no mechanism.

title: Exploring Cross-Scenario Generality of Agentic Memory Systems: Diagnostics and a Strong Baseline
notes: Cross-scenario generalization evaluation of memory systems; benchmark/diagnostic paper, no new named mechanism.

title: Language Models Need Sleep: Learning to Self-Modify and Consolidate Memories
notes: Continual-learning paper addressing "catastrophic forgetting," a long-established ML phenomenon (not newly characterized here).

title: Periodic RoPE for Infinite Context LLMs
mechanism_name: position exhaustion
is_extension_of: lost in the middle / long-context positional degradation
notes: Paper names and characterizes "position exhaustion": perplexity spikes and generation quality degrades once sequence length exceeds the positional-encoding range seen during training, distinct from (but related to) general long-context degradation.

title: MemFail: Stress-Testing Failure Modes of LLM Memory Systems
notes: Diagnostic benchmark decomposing memory-system failures into summarization/storage/retrieval error attribution; measures/attributes known failure types rather than naming a new mechanism.

title: Memory in the LLM Era: Modular Architectures and Strategies in a Unified Framework
notes: Systematic experimental comparison/survey of agent memory methods.

title: Graph-based Agent Memory: Taxonomy, Techniques, and Applications
notes: Survey of graph-based agent memory.

title: Fine-Mem: Fine-Grained Feedback Alignment for Long-Horizon Memory Management
notes: RL memory-manager training paper; reward sparsity/credit assignment is a training-methodology issue, not a context-pollution mechanism.

title: FlashMem: Distilling Intrinsic Latent Memory via Computation Reuse
notes: Latent-memory distillation architecture paper; addresses generic statelessness/redundant reprocessing.

title: Memory in Large Language Models: Mechanisms, Evaluation and Evolution
notes: Conceptual "operating system" / taxonomy paper for LLM memory research and governance; systematization, not a single new named mechanism.

title: Can Retrieval Heads See Images? Multimodal Retrieval Heads in Long-Context Vision-Language Models
notes: Mechanistic-interpretability paper extending "retrieval heads" concept to vision-language models (multimodal retrieval heads); an architectural/interpretability extension of an existing concept (retrieval heads), not itself a new degradation mechanism.

title: SEC-bench Pro: Can Language Models Solve Long-Horizon Software Security Tasks?
notes: Offensive-security (vulnerability discovery) benchmark; capability study, not an incidental mechanism.

title: Free(): Learning to Forget in Malloc-Only Reasoning Models
mechanism_name: UNNAMED: "malloc-only" context accumulation causing reasoning degeneration in extended CoT
notes: Paper diagnoses standard reasoning LLMs as "malloc-only" engines that continuously accumulate valid and redundant reasoning steps without a pruning mechanism, causing degeneration/repetitive loops and eventual reasoning collapse past a token threshold; a specific characterized architectural failure, though "malloc-only" is more a metaphor/label than an established term.

title: Multi$^2$: Hierarchical Multi-Agent Decision-Making with LLM-Based Agents in Interactive Environments
notes: Hierarchical multi-agent RL paper; "objective drift" used generically (established drift concept).

title: MEMO: Memory-Augmented Model Context Optimization for Robust Multi-Turn Multi-Agent LLM Games
notes: Multi-agent game-evaluation stability paper; run-to-run variance from compounding early deviations is a specific evaluation-methodology issue, not a context-pollution mechanism.

title: Verlog: Context-lite Multi-turn Reinforcement Learning framework for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
notes: Details empty/truncated; RL framework for long-horizon agents, no mechanism evident.

title: Mitigating Scaffolding Collapse in Socratic Tutors via Representation Alignment
mechanism_name: scaffolding collapse
notes: Central named contribution: under sustained multi-turn student pressure (persistent requests, fake mastery claims, emotional urgency, role redefinition), an LLM Socratic tutor gradually abandons guided-inquiry constraints and reveals answers directly, driven by internal representation drift. Note: threat model is framed as red-teaming/sustained user pressure, bordering on Track A; included here as the paper frames it as incidental multi-turn dialogue drift rather than a discrete attack.

title: Prompt-Activation Duality: Improving Activation Steering via Attention-Level Interventions
mechanism_name: KV-cache contamination
notes: Paper names and characterizes a specific failure of activation/persona-vector steering in stateful multi-turn dialogue: steered token states are persisted and reused via the KV cache, turning a local single-turn perturbation into cumulative coherence degradation across turns.

title: PAACE: A Plan-Aware Automated Agent Context Engineering Framework
notes: Context-engineering/compression paper; explicitly references existing "context rot" phenomenon as its motivation rather than introducing a new one.

title: CheckRLM: Effective Knowledge–Thought Coherence Checking in Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning
notes: RAG-reasoning reliability paper; addresses factual-error propagation through extended reasoning chains as a generic issue (not a new named mechanism).

title: Regime-Aware Peer Specialization for Robust RAG under Heterogeneous Knowledge Conflicts
notes: RAG robustness paper; frames a reliability spectrum (Grounding/Arbitration/Resistance) for handling heterogeneous knowledge conflicts, a categorization of existing knowledge-conflict handling rather than a new mechanism.

title: AtlasVA: Self-Evolving Visual Skill Memory for Teacher-Free VLM Agents
notes: VLM agent memory paper; names "spatial blindness" and other text-centric-memory failures for spatially-grounded agents, but these are domain-specific (visual/spatial) architecture limitations rather than a general context-pollution mechanism (details truncated).

title: Trust or Abstain? A Self-Aware RAG Approach
notes: RAG self-awareness/abstention paper; addresses knowledge-conflict miscalibration ("confident hallucination" etc.) as established failure types, not newly characterized.

title: Bridging Modalities, Spanning Time: Structured Memory for Ultra-Long Agentic Video Reasoning
notes: Ultra-long video memory-reasoning capability paper; generic evidence-discarding-before-inference limitation.

title: Lightweight LLM Agent Memory with Small Language Models
notes: Lightweight SLM-driven memory system paper; efficiency-accuracy trade-off, no new mechanism.

title: Learning When to Attend: Conditional Memory Access for Long-Context LLMs
notes: Efficient long-context architecture paper (conditional attention); addresses computational-waste inefficiency, not a degradation mechanism.

title: Research and Analysis on the Mechanism of Suppressing Large Model Hallucination Based on Modular RAG Architecture
notes: RAG hallucination-suppression mechanism-analysis paper (details truncated); studies existing hallucination phenomenon via module decomposition.

title: Enhancing Web Agents with a Hierarchical Memory Tree
notes: Web-agent memory paper; names "intention-execution entanglement" (flat memory structures conflating task logic with site-specific action details) as this system's target gap -- fairly specific engineering diagnosis, borderline but kept N as primarily describing this system's architecture limitation rather than a broadly citable phenomenon.

title: ERA: Evidence-based Reliability Alignment for Honest Retrieval-Augmented Generation
notes: RAG reliability/calibration paper; addresses epistemic vs. aleatoric uncertainty conflation under knowledge conflict, a measurement-methodology refinement not a new mechanism.

title: A-RAG: Scaling Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Hierarchical Retrieval Interfaces
notes: Agentic RAG scaling architecture paper; no new mechanism.

title: CoCoA: Confidence and Context-Aware Adaptive Decoding for Resolving Knowledge Conflicts in Large Language Models
notes: Decoding-algorithm paper (CoCoA) for knowledge-conflict resolution; no new mechanism.

title: KScope: A Framework for Characterizing the Knowledge Status of Language Models
notes: Framework for characterizing LLM "knowledge status" (taxonomy of five statuses); a measurement-methodology paper refining knowledge-conflict analysis, not introducing a new degradation mechanism.

title: Generate, Discriminate, Evolve: Enhancing Context Faithfulness via Fine-Grained Sentence-Level Self-Evolution
notes: Self-evolving training framework for context faithfulness; addresses existing knowledge-conflict/faithfulness issue at sentence granularity, not a new mechanism.

title: Reflective Planning: Vision-Language Models for Multi-Stage Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
notes: Robotic manipulation planning paper; physical/planning hallucination, off-topic from context-pollution mechanisms.

title: UniKnow: A Unified Framework for Reliable Language Model Behavior across Parametric and External Knowledge
notes: Unified reliability framework across parametric/external knowledge; taxonomizes four knowledge scenarios (an existing-conflict-adjacent categorization), not a new mechanism.

title: ReMEmbR: Building and Reasoning Over Long-Horizon Spatio-Temporal Memory for Robot Navigation
notes: Robot-navigation long-horizon memory paper; addresses generic context/memory scalability.

title: Adaptive Contrastive Decoding in Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Handling Noisy Contexts
notes: Adaptive contrastive decoding paper for noisy RAG contexts; addresses established noisy/conflicting-context robustness, no new mechanism.

title: RAT: Retrieval Augmented Thoughts Elicit Context-Aware Reasoning in Long-Horizon Generation
notes: Retrieval-augmented chain-of-thought paper; addresses generic hallucination in multi-step reasoning.

title: Who's Who: Large Language Models Meet Knowledge Conflicts in Practice
notes: Benchmark (WhoQA) for naturally-occurring knowledge conflicts from ambiguous entities; measures existing knowledge-conflict phenomenon via a new natural data source, does not introduce a new mechanism.

title: Unraveling Cross-Modality Knowledge Conflicts in Large Vision-Language Models
mechanism_name: cross-modality parametric knowledge conflict
notes: Formally defines and systematically studies a new named sub-type of knowledge conflict specific to vision-language models: inconsistency between knowledge encoded in the vision pathway vs. the language backbone, causing contradictory answers depending on modality of presentation.

title: Knowledge Conflicts for LLMs: A Survey
notes: Survey of knowledge conflicts for LLMs (three-part taxonomy); survey/synthesis of already-named phenomena.

title: Merging Generated and Retrieved Knowledge for Open-Domain QA
notes: Generate-then-read QA paper; addresses hallucinated generated passages conflicting with retrieved passages, an instance of established knowledge-conflict/hallucination framing.

title: Multi-Route Search and Adaptive Fusion for Power QA with Small Language Model Guidance
notes: Domain RAG QA paper (power systems); addresses retrieval challenges generically (details truncated).

title: Exploring Knowledge Conflicts for Faithful LLM Reasoning: Benchmark and Method
notes: Benchmark (ConflictQA) for cross-source (text-vs-KG) knowledge conflicts; an already-recognized knowledge-conflict variant, measured not newly named.

title: Parameters vs. Context: Fine-Grained Control of Knowledge Reliance in Language Models
notes: Inference-time control method (CK-PLUG) for parametric-vs-context reliance under knowledge conflict; no new mechanism.
